current.text: Rookie. Brooklyn drafted him sixth overall.
Expected to be Brooklyn's starting point guard from early in the season, ahead of most of last season's young guards. Josh is about 80% sure he starts.
Likely Brooklyn's third usage option. Julius Randle will handle the ball a lot, and coach Jordi Fernandez wants several ball handlers instead of one traditional point guard.
Could average about 5 assists and over 1 steal in about 29 to 30 minutes.
Expected to struggle as a rookie, with very high turnovers and poor percentages, mostly early in the season. Projections make FG% his weakest category at about 41.6%.
Josh projects him at 150 to 180 in both formats. Experts call him a late-round flyer, rounds 10 to 13.
If you draft him and he starts, hold him to about Thanksgiving before deciding.
He will probably be bad until around February, with minutes ramping up over the season.
Yahoo lists him as questionable with an ankle issue.
Brooklyn does not own its draft pick (it goes to Houston), so the team has no reason to tank. It is projected to be one of the worst teams, at about 28 wins.
Brooklyn is running a development season. In the second half it may give more minutes to young players, Brown among them, and Michael Porter Jr. could be traded.
Brooklyn plays 3, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21. That is only 10 games, with one back-to-back. The team has 16 back-to-backs this season, tied with Boston for the most in the league.

durable.text: Very talented point guard. He can dribble, pass and shoot, has unlimited range, dynamic athleticism and good length at 6'4 or 6'5, and shows strong passing vision. The Nets see upside on defense.
At Louisville he was a high usage guard who shot many threes, with good assists, a good steal rate and excellent free throw shooting.
At Louisville he averaged over three turnovers per game. Poor shot selection hurt his efficiency from the field and from three.
He had a back injury in college. Experts do not see it as a concern.

note: He is ranked 157 on Yahoo and 198 on ESPN, and both sites price him at 0 USD. Josh's 150 to 180 projection also puts him outside our 144-player pool, so he is at most a 1 USD last bench pick. More likely he is a waiver pickup if he starts and the assists (about 5) and steals show up. Expect early drag on FG% and turnovers, a slow build toward February and only 10 games in our playoff weeks. Check his ankle status and whether he actually starts at point guard in the first weeks before spending FAB.
